name_note: The GTDB genus Enterococcus corresponds to the classical genus; most sentences here describe Enterococcus faecalis, the species named in the cited sources.

sentences.text: Enterococcus faecalis is a human gut commensal and a major opportunistic pathogen.

A review describes it as frequently found within polymicrobial communities at biofilm-associated infection sites, including the catheterized urinary tract, surgical and chronic wounds, the gut and mucosal niches.
E. faecalis has been identified as a member of the vaginal community of healthy females, in addition to its association with vaginitis and urinary tract infections.

Vancomycin-resistant enterococci have been described as multidrug-resistant bacteria that as of 2021 continued to pervade the US healthcare system, behind Escherichia coli among healthcare-acquired infections.
A matched cohort study of 4006 febrile infants aged 90 days or younger reported Enterococcus species in 77 urine cultures, with abnormal dipstick findings less frequent than with E. coli.
